question: How do hash maps solve two-sum and frequency counting?

scenes.sub: Remember what you have seen, find it again in one step.
scenes.say: Hash maps turn a search through the whole array into one lookup. That one trick solves two sum, and a whole family of counting problems.

scenes.head: Think of a coat check
scenes.say: Think of a coat check. You hand in a coat and get a ticket. Later you show the ticket, and they fetch the coat at once. They never search the whole rack. A hash map works the same: a key leads straight to its value, in about one step on average.

scenes.head: Two sum: array 4, 1, 6, 5 and target 11
scenes.say: Array four, one, six, five. Target eleven. For each number, ask: what partner do I need? First, four. I need seven. Not in the map, so store four at index zero. Next, one. I need ten. Not there, store one. Next, six. I need five. Not there, store six. Last, five. I need six. Six is in the map at index two. Done: indices two and three.

scenes.head: Second use: counting how often each value appears
scenes.say: Second use: counting. A map from value to how many times you saw it. The line cnt of x plus plus creates a zero if the key is missing, then adds one. Then scan the map for the biggest count. Same trick solves Group Anagrams, Top K Frequent Elements, and Subarray Sum Equals K, where the key is a prefix sum. All O of n on average.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Hash the key to a bucket and jump there. Average case.
O of n if everything collides. Contests use custom hashes.
Map is a sorted tree, O of log n. Unordered is a hash.
Inserting first, so a number pairs with itself.
scenes.say: Why is lookup O of 1? You hash the key and jump to a bucket. Worst case? O of n if everything collides, so contests use custom hashes. Map versus unordered map? Map is a sorted tree, unordered is a hash. Common mistake: inserting first, so a number pairs with itself.

lines: A hash map finds a key in about one step.
Two sum: look up target minus current, then store current.
Counting: map value to count, O of n.
scenes.say: A hash map finds a key in about one step. For two sum, look up target minus the current number, then store the current one. For counting, map each value to its count. All O of n.
